description: Rows excluded from the estate because they are not permanent venues — a public space that hosts occasional temporary events is not a permanent >=1,000 venue merely because one temporary event held that many. Retained in full; nothing is deleted.

venues.name: Boucher Road Playing Fields

identity_evidence.note: Prior census provenance (workstream NORTHERN_IRELAND_03): Belfast City Council Licensing Committee report, 15 June 2022, on renewal of the 14-Day Occasional Outdoor Entertainments Licence. Gives the address "Boucher Road Playing Fields, Boucher Road, Belfast, BT12 6EU" and applicant "City and Neighbourhoods Services Dept, Belfast City Council"; states "Boucher Road Playing Fields has been used to provide large outdoor concerts for approximately 10 years" and "is owned by Belfast City Council and currently holds both a 14-Day Occasional Outdoor Entertainments Licence and a 14-Day Marquee Entertainments Licence"; sets out licensed hours; and records the special condition "Maximum numbers will be agreed at the discretion of the Building Control Service and will vary depending upon individual concert set up proposals" - the reason capacity_value is null. Also references the Ed Sheeran concert of 12 May 2022 and the AVA concerts of 24-25 September 2021.

Prior census provenance (workstream NORTHERN_IRELAND_03): Belfast City Council Licensing Committee report on outdoor events policy. Confirms Boucher Road as one of the Belfast major outdoor concert venues considered by the Licensing Committee (alongside the King's Hall and Custom House Square) and that Tennent's Vital was staged there.

calendar_evidence.note: Belfast City Council pitch-booking page; no separate public concert calendar found.

permanence_evidence.note: Belfast City Council, the controlling operator, describes the site exclusively as soccer pitches and Gaelic pitches booked through the standard pitch-booking system - no event/concert infrastructure, no venue identity of its own, no venue-hire page.
PlanetLove's run here (2021-2023, 3 editions) is real but time-bounded and not confirmed as continuing - a period of occasional/lapsed use of a public sports field, not a stable venue identity.

venues.notes: Carried forward from committed census uk-major-event-census-01 (prior venue_type=OTHER_MAJOR_EVENT_VENUE, inclusion_basis=CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED). Canonical reconciliation: no canonical venue matched by census id, exact name, name+locality, corroborated website host, or distinctive name core. [P06: permanence classified PUBLIC_SPACE_NOT_A_VENUE] [P06: excluded from the estate: not a permanent venue] [P06: Permanence review (Task 3), CORRECTED after coordinator challenge. Originally classified PERMANENT_SPORTING_GROUND with a 15,000 capacity carried over from the PlanetLove festival infobox - on re-examination this let a temporary-event figure into a permanent-sporting-ground finding through the back door, exactly the pattern the brief warns against. The council's own description (booked pitches, zero event infrastructure) and the lack of confirmed continuing recurring use both point the same way: this is honestly a public space that has hosted occasional/lapsed events, not a permanent >=1,000 venue in either a sporting or an event sense. Re-resolved to NOT_A_PERMANENT_VENUE / PUBLIC_SPACE_NOT_A_VENUE.]
